title: Turkey – Sous Vide Breast and Dark Meat Confit
description: Celebrated by chefs from Heston Blumenthal to Thomas Keller, cooking sous vide calls for slowly heating vacuum-sealed food in water at low temperatures, locking in natural juices and flavors lost with other methods. Imagine creating incredibly moist, tender turkey with no need to worry about basting or stress over timing.
ingredients: 2 turkey legs and thighs (separated and skin on)
½+ cup Duck fat, ghee, butter, olive oil
2 boneless turkey breasts (separated and skin on)
½+ cup Duck fat, ghee, butter, or olive oil
Optional aromatics, such as sprigs of rosemary or thyme
directions: Dark Meat: Combine sugar, salt, garlic, rosemary, black pepper, and duck fat in a large bowl. Add dark meat (skin on) and toss to coat. Transfer turkey legs and sugar mixture to a bag (or divide into separate bags) and seal with vacuum sealer. Add to preheated water bath and cook for 24 hours.

Turkey Breast: Place turkey breasts (skin on) in a vacuum bag with olive oil, salt, aromatics and pepper. Seal the bag and add to the sous vide bath containing the dark meat. Continue cooking at 150°F for 2 hours minimum, or up to 4 hours maximum.
Sous vide turkey can be refrigerated in their sealed bag for up to one week.
If serving after refrigeration: Arrange the top rack of your oven so it is 8 to 12 inches below the heating element, and preheat your oven to 450°F or more.
Unbag the dark meat, decanting and reserving any liquid that has accumulated for gravy.
Unbag the white meat. Arrange the dark and white meat turkey pieces, skin-side-up, on a baking sheet. Blot the pieces dry.
Roast in the very hot over or under the broiler, watching continuously, until the skin browns, about 2 to 10 minutes.
Slice the turkey breast into ½" medallions and arrange on a serving platter alongside the dark meat pieces.

You could make a little funky Mustard Citrus dressing by mixing together 4 tablespoons broth from above with ½ cup orange marmalade (slightly heated together), 2 tablespoons whole grain mustard, 2 tablespoons lime juice, 2 teaspoons or so of lime zest, a little salt, and possibly cayenne pepper to taste.
